title: A speech that fits no Christian
source_text: Εἴπερ δὲ τοιαύτη μὲν ἡ ἐν τῷ προσωποποιεῖν ἀρετὴ τοιαδὶ δὲ ἡ κακία, πῶς οὐκ εὐλόγως τις καταγελάσεται Κέλσου, Χριστιανοῖς περιτιθέντος τὰ μὴ ὑπὸ Χριστιανῶν λεγόμενα; εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἰδιωτῶν ἀνέπλασσε λόγους, πόθεν τοῖς τοιούτοις δύνασθαι διακρίνειν αἴσθησιν ἀπὸ τοῦ νοῦ καὶ αἰσθητὰ νοητῶν καὶ δογματίζειν παραπλησίως τοῖς ἀναιροῦσι νοητὰς οὐσίας Στωϊκοῖς περὶ τοῦ αἰσθήσεσιν καταλαμβάνεσθαι τὰ καταλαμβανόμενα καὶ πᾶσαν κατάληψιν ἠρτῆσθαι τῶν αἰσθήσεων; εἰ δ᾿ ἀναπλάσσει λόγους τῶν φιλοσοφούντων καὶ ἐπιμελῶς ὅση δύναμις ἐξεταζόντων τὰ Χριστοῦ. οὐδὲ τούτοις ἀκόλουθα πεποίηκεν. οὐδεὶς γὰρ μαθὼν ἀόρατον εἶναι τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶναί τινα δημιουργήματα ἀόρατα. τουτέστι νοητὰ, λέγοι ἂν ὡς ἀπολογούμενος περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τό· πῶς αἰσθήσεσι μὴ καταλαμβανόμενοι γνώσονται τὸν θεόν; ἤ· τί χωρὶς αἰσθήσεως μαθεῖν δυνατόν ἐστι; καὶ οὐκ ἐν ἀνακεχωρηκόσι καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένοις ὑπὸ ὀλίγων μόνον καὶ φιλομαθῶν ἀλλ᾿ ἐν τοῖς δημωδεστέροις γέγραπται ὅτι „τὰ ἀόρατα τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασι νοούμενα καθορᾶται“· δι᾿ ὧν ἔστιν εἰδέναι ὅτι εἰ καὶ τοὺς ἐν βίῳ ἀνθρώπους χρὴ ἀπὸ αἰσθήσεων ἄρξασθαι καὶ τῶν αἰσθητῶν, μέλλοντας ἀναβαίνειν ἐπὶ τὴν τῶν νοητῶν φύσιν, ἀλλ᾿ οὔτι γε ἐν αἰσθητοῖς καταμένειν χρή· οὔτε χωρὶς αἰσθήσεως ἐροῦσιν ἀδύνατον εἶναι μαθεῖν τὰ νοητὰ, χρώμενοι δὲ τῷ τίς χωρὶς αἰσθήσεως μαθεῖν δυνατός ἐστιν; ἐλέγξουσιν οὐκ εὐλόγως τούτῳ ὑπὸ τοῦ Κέλσου ἐπιφέρεσθαι τὸ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου μὲν οὐδὲ ψυχῆς ἀλλὰ γὰρ σαρκὸς φωνή.
pass_a_gloss: If such is the virtue (ἀρετή) in personifying (προσωποποιέω) and such the vice (κακία), how will one not reasonably (εὐλόγως) laugh at (καταγελάω) Celsus, attributing to Christians things not said by Christians? For if he fashioned (ἀναπλάσσω) words of laymen (ἰδιώτης), whence could such distinguish (διακρίνω) sense (αἴσθησις) from mind (νοῦς), sensibles (αἰσθητά) from intelligibles (νοητά), and dogmatise (δογματίζω) like the Stoics (Στωϊκοί) who abolish (ἀναιρέω) intelligible substances (νοηταὶ οὐσίαι), that things apprehended (καταλαμβάνω) are apprehended by senses and all apprehension (κατάληψις) depends on (ἀρτάω) the senses? If he fashions words of those philosophising and carefully examining (ἐξετάζω), as far as power allows, the things of Christ, he has not made consistent (ἀκόλουθος) things for these either. For no one having learned God is invisible (ἀόρατος) and there are invisible creations (δημιούργημα), that is, intelligibles, would say as defending (ἀπολογέομαι) about resurrection: how, not apprehending by senses, will they know God? or: what is possible to learn without sense? And not in withdrawn (ἀνακεχωρηκότα, i.e. esoteric) writings read by few and studious (φιλομαθής), but in the more popular (δημώδης) it is written that the invisible things of God from creation (κτίσις) of the world, understood (νοέω) by the things made (ποίημα), are seen clearly (καθοράω); through which one may know that even if those in life must begin (ἄρχομαι) from senses and sensibles, being about to ascend (ἀναβαίνω) to the nature (φύσις) of intelligibles, yet they must not at all remain (καταμένω) in sensibles; nor will they say it is impossible to learn intelligibles without sense, but using 'who is able to learn without sense?' they will refute (ἐλέγχω) as unreasonable Celsus's adding (ἐπιφέρω) to this: not of a man nor soul but of flesh the voice.
pass_b_english: If, then, such is the merit in writing speeches for characters and such the fault, who could not laugh at Celsus, and with good reason, when he puts into the mouths of Christians things that Christians do not say? For if he was making up the words of simple folk, how could such people distinguish sense from mind and the objects of sense from the objects of thought, and teach, like the Stoics who do away with intelligible realities, that whatever is grasped is grasped by the senses and that all grasping depends on the senses? But if he is making up the words of those who study philosophy and who examine carefully, as far as they are able, the things of Christ, he has not given them words that fit them either.

For no one who has learned that God is invisible, and that there are some invisible created things, that is, intelligible ones (Colossians 1:15–16), would say, as though in defence of the resurrection: “How will they know God if they do not grasp him by the senses?” or “What can be learned without sense?” And it is written, not in writings kept apart and read only by a few lovers of learning, but in the more commonly read ones, that “the invisible things of God, from the creation of the world, are clearly seen, being understood through the things that are made” (Romans 1:20). From this we may know that, even if people in this life must begin from the senses and the objects of sense when they are going to rise up to the nature of intelligible things, they must certainly not remain among the objects of sense. Nor will they say that it is impossible to learn intelligible things without sense; and if they do use the words “Who can learn without sense?”, they will show that Celsus had no good reason to add to them “the voice not of a man, nor of the soul, but of the flesh.”

choices.choice: ‘ἀόρατον εἶναι τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶναί τινα δημιουργήματα ἀόρατα’ alludes to Colossians 1:15 (‘the image of the invisible God’) and 1:16 (things ‘visible and invisible’ created in him); cited inline. Romans 1:20 quoted in Paul’s wording (τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται), with ‘τοῦ θεοῦ’ for ‘αὐτοῦ’. ‘οὐκ ἐν ἀνακεχωρηκόσι ... ἀλλ᾿ ἐν τοῖς δημωδεστέροις’ contrasts secluded (esoteric) books with the more widely circulated ones, i.e. Paul’s letters; rendered ‘writings kept apart ... more commonly read ones’. ‘τί’ (7.36) appears here as ‘τίς’ in the last requotation (‘Who can learn ...’); translated as transmitted. The final sentence is compressed: ‘χρώμενοι δὲ τῷ ...’ is read as conditional/concessive (‘and if they do use the words’), i.e. even a Christian who used the phrase would mean only that learning begins from sense. καταλαμβάνω/κατάληψις rendered ‘grasp/grasping’ to keep the Stoic technical sense (cognitive apprehension) recognisable without a calque.

οὐδὲ τούτοις ἀκόλουθα πεποίηκεν: stiff 'made what he gives them consistent with them' changed to 'has not given them words that fit them either'

δημωδεστέροις: 'more widely known' changed to 'more commonly read'
